title: The same reason then
hook: don't be troubled by the future; you'll meet it with the same reason you have now (Meditations 7.8)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the snake-catcher and his frozen dragon, woken by the sun. Your line was careful in the sun. Did you stay a step away from yours? Day two hundred five.

It's 2am. The house is quiet, and your mind is running a movie of next month. The meeting where it all goes wrong. The bill you can't pay. The phone call from the doctor. You play it three different ways, and every version, you're alone and unprepared. Here's the strange thing: in the movie, the person facing the future is a weaker, more confused version of you. Somehow we imagine that when the hard day comes, we'll show up with nothing. Marcus had a short answer to 2am. Today: the same reason then.
screen: `2AM, THE MOVIE OF NEXT MONTH.` → `A WEAKER VERSION OF YOU.` → `THE SAME REASON THEN.`

segments.voice: Book Seven, section eight, in George Long's translation: "Let not future things disturb thee, for thou wilt come to them, if it shall be necessary, having with thee the same reason which now thou usest for present things." Look at the three pieces. First: let not future things disturb you. Not: the future won't be hard. It might be. Just: don't let it trouble you now. Second: if it shall be necessary. Some of what we dread never arrives. Marcus doesn't promise that, but he leaves the door open. Third, the heart of it: you'll bring with you the same reason you're using today. Reason, for the Stoics, meant more than logic. It meant the whole power in you to see clearly, choose well and act rightly. And it's portable. You carry it everywhere. Whatever you use today to handle the dishes, the emails and the hard conversation, you'll have tomorrow too. The 2am movie always forgets this. It sends a helpless you into the future. Marcus says it'll be the same you, with the same tools, and probably more practice. And that gathers up our week of seeing clearly. The purple robe was only wool and shellfish. The emperor refused to be dyed a Caesar. The bee belongs to the hive. Our palms are small on the elephant. The call was already the answer. The dragon was only frozen. And the future is met by the same mind you have now. Your line: the same reason then.
screen: `LET NOT FUTURE THINGS DISTURB THEE.` · `IF IT SHALL BE NECESSARY.` · `THE SAME REASON YOU USE NOW.` · then, large: `THE SAME REASON THEN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: leave one future worry for later. Settle, and let one worry about the future come up. Look at it once. Then picture yourself, on that day, with the same mind and the same care you have right now, maybe with a friend beside you. Say inside: I'll meet it then. And set it down for these two minutes. If it comes back, just say it again. The bell holds the time.
The same reason then. Marcus says don't be troubled by the future: you'll meet it with the same reason you use today. Today's word.
Your line: the same reason then. Today, when the worry comes back, say the line and turn to the thing in front of you right now. Day two hundred five.

howItsDone: Many readers of the Stoics use this line at night or in anxious moments, reminding themselves that the same judgment and care they have today will be there when the future arrives.

original.note: Greek: reason, word, account. the Stoics' word for the reasoning power in us, and in the universe.

trapdoor: what you thought: don't think about the future.
what it means: you'll meet the future with the same mind you have today, so it needn't trouble you now.
what a scholar hears: logos, for the Stoics both the reason in each person and the reason that orders the cosmos, which is why it can't be left behind.
